function:rack::widget::getKeyCommandName.finding: P2: Rack's default argument is not honoured. The SDK declares getKeyCommandName(int key, int mods = 0) (include/widget/event.hpp:56). The binding at native/bindings/widget/templates.cpp:146-149 registers py::arg("mods") with no default, and the stub src/rackpy/raw/widget.pyi:674 has 'mods: int', so get_key_command_name(65) raises TypeError. This is contrary to docs/coverage.md policy 6 ('Default arguments are recorded and honoured'). Smallest fix: use py::arg("mods") = 0, change the stub to 'mods: int = 0', and add the assertion get_key_command_name(65) == 'A' in check_key_names (tests/widget/in_rack/test_templates.py:17).

method:rack::widget::EventState::handleT.finding: P2: An undocumented and unjustified restriction. native/bindings/ui/event_state.cpp:127-128 raises ValueError for codepoint > 0x10FFFF, but Rack's EventState::handleText(math::Vec, uint32_t) accepts any uint32_t and only forwards it in Hover/SelectText events (Rack src/widget/event.cpp). Neither the manifest notes nor docs/reference/ui.md#ui-input mention the restriction or a crash or undefined behaviour that would justify it. Smallest fix: remove the check, or document it in ui.md with Rack-source evidence that such values are unsafe, and add a test for it.

method:rack::widget::ZoomWidget::draw(co.finding: P1: No cited test runs ZoomWidget::draw, which applies nvgScale(zoom) and rescales the clip box. tests/widget/in_rack/test_drawing.py draws only through Widget and FramebufferWidget, with no ZoomWidget anywhere in the file. test_variants.py::test_every_variant_subclass_round_trip_and_native_step only steps a ZoomWidget, and test_transparent_opaque_and_zoom_event_base_semantics only sends hover events. Smallest fix: render a FramebufferWidget that contains a ZoomWidget with set_zoom(2) and a Python child whose draw records args.clip_box. Assert the clip box is divided by the zoom, and also call ZoomWidget.draw through super().

method:rack::widget::ZoomWidget::drawLay.finding: P1: No cited test reaches ZoomWidget::drawLayer. test_drawing.py:22-73 calls draw_layer only through Widget.draw_child on a plain Widget parent, and none of the cited test_variants.py tests draws. Smallest fix: in the zoomed-render test proposed for ZoomWidget::draw, call draw_child(zoom_widget, args, 1) or super().draw_layer(args, 1). Assert that the child's draw_layer receives the layer and a zoom-scaled clip_box.

method:rack::widget::ZoomWidget::getView.finding: P1: No test calls get_viewport on a ZoomWidget or through one. In tests/, get_viewport appears only in tests/widget/in_rack/test_tree.py:309-310, on the detached WidgetNode adapter. Smallest fix: in test_transparent_opaque_and_zoom_event_base_semantics, assert parent.get_viewport(rect) and child.get_viewport(rect) under set_zoom(2) against Rack's expected scaled rectangle.

method_template:rack::widget::Widget::ge.finding: P1: Unjustified restriction, and the notes are misleading. matcher() at native/bindings/widget/templates.cpp:20-43 uses rttiCast only for the 8 rack::widget classes (lines 24-33). Every other bound SDK widget class goes to the managed-peer isinstance branch (lines 37-43), which returns false for widgets RackPy does not manage. Examples are rackpy.raw.app.ModuleWidget, which is an OpaqueWidget subclass (native/bindings/app/module_widget.cpp:219), RackWidget and ui classes. So get_ancestor_of_type(app.ModuleWidget) returns None for a Rack-owned ModuleWidget, where Rack's dynamic_cast<T*>(parent) (include/widget/Widget.hpp getAncestorOfType) finds it. The manifest notes say 'the bound SDK classes match by dynamic_cast' and the stub returns T | HostWidget (widget.pyi:453), but tests/widget/in_rack/test_templates.py:37-74 only uses rack::widget classes. Policy 10 requires templates over widget types to accept any class. Smallest fix: match every pybind-registered SDK widget class by its C++ type, for example a registry of rttiCast matchers filled in by variant<>. Then add an in-Rack test that finds a Rack-owned app class, such as the RuntimeProbe ModuleWidget.

P1: Same matcher restriction as getAncestorOfType. native/bindings/widget/templates.cpp:20-43 and descendantOf at lines 53-61 use dynamic_cast only for the 8 rack::widget classes. The notes ('matched as for get_ancestor_of_type') and the stub widget.pyi:454 (T | HostWidget) suggest that it does. Tests use only rack::widget classes (test_templates.py:57-59).
